query: what does section 159 of Indian Evidence Act cover?
answer_simple: Section 159 of the Indian Evidence Act lets a witness use notes or documents to help remember things. The witness can look at their own notes or someone else's notes if they read them and know they're right. If a witness can say they're sure the notes are correct, they can use them to tell the truth about things they can't remember well.

query: what does section 135 of Indian Evidence Act cover?
answer_simple: Section 135 of the Indian Evidence Act says the judge decides the order in which witnesses are asked questions. It's about how and when people who know about the case are questioned.
answer_legal: [IEA_s135] Section 135 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, deals with the order of production and examination of witnesses. It states that the order in which witnesses are produced and examined shall be regulated by the law and practice for the time being relating to civil and criminal procedure respectively, and in the absence of any such law, by the discretion of the Court.

query: what does section 23 of Income-tax Act cover?
answer_simple: Section 23 of the Income-tax Act says that if you get late rent or money you're owed from a tenant, it counts as income for tax purposes. It also lets you take a 30% cut from that income. This applies whether you own the property or not.
answer_legal: [ITA2025_s23] Section 23 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, deals with the treatment of arrears of rent and unrealised rent received subsequently. It states that the amount of arrears of rent or unrealised rent received by an assessee from a tenant shall be deemed to be the income from house property in the tax year in which such rent is received or realised. The amount deemed to be income from house property under this section shall be included in the total income of the assessee under the head 'Income from house property', whether the assessee is the owner of the property or not in that tax year.

query: what does section 59 of Code on Wages cover?
